permutationLabel: High-risk PE with shock, active cancer
summary: 68-year-old man with pancreatic cancer on chemotherapy, collapsed at home: SBP 82, HR 128, RR 30, SpO₂ 86 %, raised JVP. ESC 2019 high-risk PE: UFH, bedside echo, systemic thrombolysis.

inputs.hpi: Known locally advanced pancreatic cancer on gemcitabine, under our follow-up after biliary stenting. Collapsed at home this morning after getting up; now severely breathless at rest and grey. No chest pain. Right calf swollen for a week.

exam.cardiovascular: HR 128 regular, BP 82/50, JVP raised to the earlobe, loud P2.

surgicalHistory: ERCP and biliary metal stent 2 months ago

confirmedDiagnosis.name: High-risk (massive) pulmonary embolism
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism with shock and RV strain in active cancer: resuscitation, UFH, bedside echocardiography, systemic thrombolysis if RV dysfunction confirmed.

mustInclude.note: Bedside echo when CTPA is not immediately feasible in suspected high-risk PE.
Systemic thrombolysis for high-risk PE (ESC 2019, class I).
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no thrombolysis anywhere. The confirmed ICD I26.09 (PE with acute cor pulmonale, i.e. the high-risk PE code) has no getProtocolByIcd mapping (I26.9/I26.99 do), and the PANE top is not PE, so the PE protocol, which lists alteplase, is never shown. Management comes only from the shock/hypoxia/tachycardia prompts: "Hartmann's 1L bolus", "12-lead ECG", "CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2".
mustInclude.proposedFix: Map I26.0x (PE with acute cor pulmonale) to the pulmonary_embolism protocol; in the shock prompt, when PE is suspected (hypoxia + raised JVP/DVT signs), add "high-risk PE: UFH, bedside echo, systemic thrombolysis".

mustExclude.note: ESC 2019: aggressive volume expansion can worsen RV function; cautious volume loading only.

guideline.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism
guideline.section: Sections 4-6: clinical probability (Wells/Geneva), PERC in low probability, D-dimer only when probability is not high, CTPA; anticoagulation while awaiting results in high/intermediate probability; high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE: UFH, bedside echocardiography if CTPA not immediately feasible, systemic thrombolysis; Section 9 pregnancy: D-dimer/CUS/CTPA or V/Q, LMWH (NOACs not recommended in pregnancy)
guideline.citation: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. Eur Heart J. 2020;41:543-603.

rationale: High-risk PE: obstructive shock in active cancer. Tests whether the web shock prompt and the PE protocol reach thrombolysis, and whether a generic 1 L bolus is suggested.

authoring.author: Claude (acute medicine cluster)
